full_judgment:
2. The case of the plaintiff, in short, is that the deceased Ganzer Molla, father of defendant Nos. 1 to 3 and his wife defendant No.4 filed Title Suit No. 179 of 1965 in the court of the Subordinate Judge against the plaintiff and others. Plaintiff appeared in that suit and filed a written statement but ultimately that suit was compromised out of court between the plaintiff and the aforesaid Ganzer Molla and his wife and that suit was decreed in terms of the petition of compromise or solenama. That solenama provided that the present plaintiff relinquished his claim in respect of 1.04 acres of suit land of that Title Suit No. 179 of 1965 and plaintiffs of that suit agreed to execute and register a kabala in respect of 0.60 acre of their other land as consideration of that Solenama within a month from the date of compromise. Further case of the plaintiff is, that the plaintiffs of Title Suit No. 179 of 1965 took delivery of possession of the said 1.04 acres of land from the present plaintiff but they did not execute and register kabala in favour of the present plaintiff in respect of the aforesaid 0.60 acre of land (suit land of the present suit) in spite of repeated demands of the present plaintiff. Subsequently, said Ganzer Molla died leaving defendants 1 to 4 as his legal heirs. So the plaintiff demanded execution and registration of the kabala from the present defendants on 20th Ashar, 1376 BS for the last time, but his demand having been refused he filed Title Suit No. 135 of 1969 for specific performance for getting a kabala. 

 3. Defendant No. 1 alone appeared and contested the suit by filing a written statement denying material allegations of the plaint and stating, inter alia that the suit is not maintainable in the present form. Further case of the defendant No. 1 is that the plaintiff obtained the alleged compromise decree in Title Suit No. 179 by practising fraud upon the court. The suit land belonged to Ganzer Molla predecessor of the defendant who possessed the same as his heir. Ganzer Molla and his wife present defendant No. 4, did not file Title Suit No. 179 of 1965 against the present plaintiff and others and there was no reason to file such a suit and also there was no reason on the part of the defendant No. 1 as his first son not to know about that suit. The present plaintiff by false personification through his own man had filed that suit and by practising fraud upon the court obtained a compromise decree on the basis of solenama dated 1.8.66 illegally including the lands which were not subject matter of that suit by forging signature of Ganzer Molla and the present defendant did not dare to file any suit during life time of Ganzer Molla and kept the forged solenama suppressed during life time of Ganzer Molla and filed the suit after his death to injure the defendant. 

 6. Fraud is a mixed question of fact and law. Court of appeal below on consideration of the evidence came to the finding "I am inclined to believe that solenama filed in the aforesaid Title Suit No. 179 of 1965 was genuine and it was filed by Ganzer Molla and his wife respondent No. 4 of this appeal and as such she did not come forward to deny the solenama in question nor does she contest this appeal before this court Having regard to all these facts and circumstances and the evidence on record I find that Ganzer Molla and his wife who is respondent No. 4 in this appeal, filed Title Suit No. 179 of 1965 which suit was compromised in terms of the solenama filed by them with the present plaintiff and by that compromise Ganzer Molla and his wife contracted to transfer the suit land to the present plaintiff.
